items.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996
items.q: And I used to do, I did all the Belafonte dates, you know, recording sessions.

ctx.x: Any percussion sound. Oh that Milt, dear sweet Milt. He’s not too well these days unfortunately. But we became very close friends. But those were such wonderful, wonderful days. And then one of the writers on the Carson Show was Dick Cavett. And I had been doing recording sessions. And Harry Belafonte, remember “The Banana Boat © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -5-

Song?” “Day-Oh.” Well I always liked Latin drums and things and bongos and conga drums. So I kind of, since I could read music, and that was never a problem, I never thought about it, I just did it. So I was one of the few quote long hair players, capable of playing that that could also do the other stuff. And I didn’t do it because oh I’m going to show you sort of thing, I just did it because you do that. And I used to do, I did all the Belafonte dates, you know, recording sessions.
